questions.prompt: A microscope has a 10× eyepiece and a 40× objective lens. What is the total magnification?
Order the steps for viewing an onion peel slide.
steps: Peel a thin, transparent layer from the inside of an onion scale
Place it flat in a drop of water on a slide and add a drop of iodine
Lower a cover slip gently at an angle to avoid air bubbles
Start with the lowest-power objective and focus with the coarse knob
Switch to a higher-power objective and sharpen with the fine focus
questions.explain: Always start on low power, then move to high power.

questions.prompt: Who first used the word ‘cell’, after looking at thin slices of cork in 1665?
questions.explain: The empty cork compartments reminded Hooke of small rooms (cells).

questions.prompt: The field of view is 4500 µm across, and about 18 onion cells fit across it end to end. Estimate the length of one cell.
In the Virtual Microscope, what happened to the field of view when you switched from 100× to 400×?
options: It got smaller: you see less of the slide, but in more detail
questions.explain: Four times the magnification gives a field of view a quarter as wide.

questions.prompt: Why do we add iodine or methylene blue to a slide?
options: To stain parts like the nucleus so they can be seen more clearly
questions.explain: Most cell parts are nearly transparent until stained.

questions.prompt: How many micrometres (µm) are there in 1 millimetre?
questions.explain: 1 mm = 1000 µm. Most cells are 10–100 µm across.

questions.prompt: Plan how you would prepare and view a slide of your own cheek cells safely and clearly.
questions.modelAnswer: Rinse your mouth. Gently scrape the inside of your cheek with a clean toothpick or cotton bud. Smear it in a drop of water on a clean slide and add a drop of methylene blue stain. Lower a cover slip at an angle to avoid air bubbles and blot extra stain with tissue paper. View on the lowest power first, focus, then switch to higher power and refocus with the fine knob. Dispose of the toothpick safely and wash your hands.
rubric: Low power first, then high power
questions.explain: Criterion B: a clear, safe method.
